props.text: Practical logistics on airports, direct bookings and family stays—plus a 48-hour courtesy hold while you confirm flights to Menorca.

items.a: Dune House sleeps up to six across three bedrooms (two king suites and one twin room) and suits families or friends who want expansive terrace dining above the sea. Blue Shutter Cottage sleeps four in the village of Fornells where you can walk everywhere. Sa Caleta Casita is designed for a couple seeking quiet seclusion among olive trees.
items.q: Which home is best suited for our group size and pace?

items.a: Send us your preferred home, target dates and group size through our stay inquiry form. Host founder Mateu Serra replies within 24 hours with confirmed availability, an itemized seasonal quote including local ecotax, and a direct reservation agreement with zero third-party platform fees.
items.q: How do direct reservations and seasonal availability work?

items.a: All three homes are between 20 and 28 minutes by car from Mahón Airport (MAH). While Blue Shutter Cottage sits right in Fornells village with bus and boat connections, we recommend a compact rental car for exploring hidden north- and south-shore trailheads.
items.q: Do we need a car on Menorca, and how far are the homes from Mahón Airport?

items.a: Every stay includes washed Belgian flax bed linens, Turkish beach towels, straw market baskets, insulated cove coolers, cedar kayaks or paddleboards, and an arrival pantry of estate olive oil, local wine, Mahón cheese, orchard fruit and crusty bread.
items.q: What is included in the house pantry and beach equipment?

props.alt: Limestone dining terrace overlooking coastal dunes and the Mediterranean sea in morning light

props.text: Perched above the pine-fringed dunes of Es Grau on Menorca’s northeastern nature reserve, wrapping three vaulted limestone bedrooms around a sixty-foot sea terrace.
Morning light over the water, afternoon shade beneath sabina beams.

At Dune House, the sixty-foot limestone terrace sets the cadence of the day. Breakfast runs late around the ten-foot chestnut table, afternoon swims end at the warm brushed-copper garden shower, and evenings gather around the wood-fired stone plancha.
Two king suites plus a convertible twin bedroom opening straight onto louvered stone terraces.
Monolithic limestone indoor island paired with a shaded outdoor stone sink and wood plancha.
Two coastal kayaks wait by the dune gate for flat morning paddles out to Illa d’en Colom.
Rinse sandy feet beneath warm rain water surrounded by rosemary and dry-stone walls.

props.alt: Whitewashed Blue Shutter Cottage exterior with painted cobalt shutters along a quiet coastal village lane

props.text: Tucked along a quiet pedestrian limestone lane in the northern fishing village of Fornells, pairing whitewashed vaulted salons with a walled citrus breakfast courtyard.
Walk two minutes for morning bread, return to cool limewashed stone.

Blue Shutter Cottage was restored for guests who love the walkable cadence of a Menorcan harbor village. Stroll to the waterfront for warm ensaïmadas, hike out along Cap de Cavalleria, and linger afternoon hours beside the courtyard lemon fountain.
High limewashed walls enclose a private garden court with mature lemon trees and crimson bougainvillea.
Hand-scraped beams and reclaimed floor tiles hold cool shade all through August afternoons.
Board skipper Pau Cardona’s restored 32-foot wooden boat two minutes down Calle de la Marina.
Two minutes to the fish quay and eight minutes on foot to flat limestone harbor swimming rocks.
2 min to waterfront · 8 min to swim rocks

props.alt: Mediterranean limestone cove with clear turquoise water and a stone house among pine trees

props.text: A coastline of quiet calas and working harbors.
Protected from high-rise resort development since 1993, Menorca preserves ancient coastal footpaths, pine-sheltered swimming coves and small island farms.
Morning swims, pergola lunches, harbor markets, and coastal trails.
Every Salt House residence comes with printed wind charts so you can pick the calmest cove each morning.

props.alt: Quiet turquoise Mediterranean limestone cove in early morning sunlight with wooden kayak on flat rocks

props.text: First water on quiet limestone shallows.
Step down our private footpath ten minutes before breakfast with a flask of coffee and launch a cedar kayak across glass-calm morning bays.
Two coastal kayaks and dry bags are stored beside Dune House’s lower gate.
Swim Cala Presili or Es Grau bay when southerly breezes flatten the north shore.
Return straight to our outdoor brushed-copper garden shower among wild rosemary.

props.alt: Shaded outdoor lunch table beneath an olive tree overlooking the Mediterranean coast

props.text: Three-hour lunches beneath woven cane and wild olive.
Every Salt House terrace centers on an outdoor summer kitchen—built around ten-seat chestnut or stone tables, wood-fired planchas and chilled island white wine.
Arrive to our stocked kitchen larder: estate olive oil, Mahón cheese, wood-oven bread and sea salt.
Order morning red mullet and prawns directly from the Fornells harbor boats via Aina.
Every residence provides handmade ceramic serving platters, ice buckets and outdoor speakers.

props.alt: Sunlit coastal village morning market stand with woven baskets of heirloom tomatoes, figs, bread and olive oil

props.text: Cloister markets, harbor bakeries, and sunset paseos.
Stroll from Blue Shutter Cottage at 8:30 for warm pastries, visit Maó’s morning fish cloister under seventeenth-century stone arches, and browse weekly island stalls.
Explore Blue Shutter Cottage in Fornells
Maó Claustre del Carme covers fresh fish, Mahón curado cheese and figs Tue–Sat mornings.
Alaior & Es Mercadal evening artisan markets showcase hand-thrown Menorcan stoneware.
Woven palm senalla baskets and linen produce bags hang inside every Salt House entry hall.

props.alt: Camí de Cavalls coastal stone path winding along dry-stone walls above a calm deep-blue sea in autumn light

props.text: The Camí de Cavalls in golden shoulder-season light.
Between April and June or September through November, the ancient 185-kilometer coastal bridal path links red-sand headlands, pine ravines and warm sea water without summer crowds.
Direct trailhead access onto Stage 3 (Es Grau) and Stage 7 (Cavalleria) from our gates.
Mediterranean sea temperature remains near 22°C through late October.
Olive-wood fireplaces and radiant underfloor heating keep autumn evenings effortlessly warm.
Driving and walking times from each residence.

props.text: Everything to know before you pack.

items.a: Submit your preferred home and target dates in the inquiry form above. Because many of our returning guests book flexible 5- to 10-day windows, Mateu checks the calendar personally and sends a 48-hour courtesy hold along with your itemized rate sheet.
items.q: How do I check live dates and confirm a booking?

items.a: Yes. Skipper Pau Cardona reserves four days each week exclusively for Salt House guests. You can request a half-day morning cove swim or a full-day north-shore picnic charter when you book your residence.
items.q: Can we charter the Salt House wooden llaüt boat during our stay?

items.a: Es Grau bay (four minutes on foot from Dune House) is one of the shallowest, most sheltered sandy bays in the Mediterranean, remaining knee- to waist-deep for fifty meters from shore. Always check daily flag and wind conditions.
items.q: Is the swimming water safe for children near the homes?

items.a: Yes. All three residences are equipped with symmetrical 600 Mbps fiber or Starlink broadband and quiet writing desks with natural window light.
